project: SAC S0.1 — Restore Package-Target and Ownership Inventories to the Live Tree
description: Restore the package-target manifest, ownership inventory, architecture guards, and canonical service-owner documentation so every live production package and cross-owner dependency has one reviewed owner and classification, unresolved bidirectional edges remain visible, and provider inference and hosted polling are assigned to Providers and Automations rather than Workers.

context.customerAsk: Implement story S0.1 of the Service Abstraction Convergence plan: regenerate and review the package-target manifest and ownership inventory; add the missing Worker Sessions, Events, Chat Sessions, ACP, Factory Sessions, Providers, platform, and mapping packages; correct the eight guards and documentation entries that misassign provider inference or hosted polling to Workers; and reconcile the service-owner tables in AGENTS.md, docs/architecture/architecture.md, and docs/architecture/packaged-structure.md.
context.problem: The checked-in architecture inventories and some enforcement and documentation surfaces lag the live production package graph. Missing packages and edges, future-tense rationale for implemented services, and incorrect Workers ownership assignments prevent maintainers from trusting the inventories as a statement of package ownership, dependency direction, and remaining convergence debt.
context.solution: Regenerate deterministic inventory candidates from the current production tree, review every package and cross-owner edge against durable service boundaries, preserve unresolved bidirectional dependencies as visible debt, correct inference and polling ownership guards, and align the three canonical service-owner tables without changing runtime behavior or widening into unrelated package migrations.

acceptanceCriteria: make package-target-manifest-check passes from a clean checkout.
make ownership-inventory-check passes and reports no missing production package or cross-owner edge.

Every live production package appears exactly once with a durable owner or the explicit Process Edges exception, including Worker Sessions, Events, Chat Sessions, ACP, Factory Sessions, Providers, platform, and mapping packages.
Inventory regeneration does not silently reclassify a bidirectional edge as acceptable; every unresolved bidirectional edge remains visible until its owning convergence story lands.

The eight affected guards and documentation entries assign provider inference to Providers and hosted polling to Automations, and the service-owner tables in AGENTS.md, architecture.md, and packaged-structure.md state the same durable ownership model.
Typecheck and relevant focused tests pass; no NEW lint violations relative to current main, and the gates green on main (backend-size, pkg-maint, pkg-file-count, pkg-structure, vet) stay green.

The implementation/review loop continues until required CI is terminal and passing, all blocking PR conversation feedback is explicitly addressed, merge conflicts are resolved against current main, and the PR is actually merged.

acceptanceCriteria: Regeneration accounts for every live production package exactly once as a reviewed retain or move destination, with only the explicit Process Edges exception outside durable service or family ownership.

Worker Sessions, Events, Chat Sessions, ACP, Factory Sessions, Providers, platform, and mapping package families present in the live tree are represented with destinations consistent with the repository architecture.
make package-target-manifest-check passes from a clean checkout and fails in a focused regression case when a production package is missing or duplicated.

Tests pass

userStories.notes: Regenerated the package-target manifest from the live production Go tree (545 packages) and retained the 17 newly discovered paths under platform, Chat Sessions, Events, Factory Sessions, Providers, Worker Sessions, ACP, CLI, and mapping destinations. Added Worker Sessions to the closed package-target owner vocabulary and reconciled the live Chat Sessions/Events/Worker Sessions top-level inventories. userStories.description: As an architecture reviewer, I want every production package and cross-owner dependency to have a reviewed owner and relationship classification so that dependency direction and remaining convergence debt are explicit.
acceptanceCriteria: The ownership inventory covers every production package from the regenerated package-target manifest and reports no missing or duplicate ownership row.

Every live cross-owner dependency is reviewed and classified as command, query, event, construction, lifecycle, protocol composition, or external effect, with a rationale consistent with the owning service contract.
Worker Sessions, Events, Chat Sessions, ACP, Factory Sessions, Providers, platform, and mapping packages and their live cross-owner edges are included.
Chat Sessions and Events rationale describes their implemented ownership and behavior in the present tense rather than as future work.
Regeneration preserves every unresolved bidirectional edge as visible debt and a focused regression test proves that such an edge cannot be silently reclassified as acceptable.
make ownership-inventory-check passes and reports no missing production package or edge.
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Regenerated the ownership inventory from the live package graph (576 existing-scope package rows) and added the 16 package-target paths introduced by story 001, including Worker Sessions, Events, Chat Sessions, ACP, Factory Sessions, Providers, platform, and mapping paths. Added Worker Sessions to the closed owner vocabulary, top-level inventory, and rationale cards; rewrote Chat Sessions and Events rationale in the present tense. Cross-owner discovery now records 155 classified edges, marks all 50 directed entries in reciprocal pairs as unresolved bidirectional debt, and rejects a valid interaction class when those debt markers are removed. make ownership-inventory-check, focused ownership tests, package-target-manifest-check, and git diff --check pass. The full internal ownership package still reports pre-existing Workers/Recordings root-contract baseline drift unrelated to this story.

userStories.title: Correct inference and hosted-polling ownership enforcement
userStories.description: As a service owner, I want architecture enforcement to attribute provider inference and hosted polling to their durable owners so that new code cannot deepen the incorrect Workers boundary.
acceptanceCriteria: All eight affected guard and documentation entries are reviewed and corrected: provider inference is assigned to Providers, hosted polling is assigned to Automations, and Workers retains only its request-scoped execution responsibilities.

Ownership rationale distinguishes Workers deciding when to execute a worker attempt from Providers owning provider protocol, selection, session, adapter, and execution behavior, and from Automations owning hosted-source observation and polling.
Focused guard tests reject a new production assignment of provider inference or hosted polling to Workers while accepting the reviewed Providers and Automations ownership paths.
No runtime behavior, public API contract, or unrelated Workers migration is changed by this correction.
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Corrected the package-boundary owner metadata for Providers execution/adapters and rewrote the provider-effect diagnostics to distinguish Providers-owned protocol, selection, session, adapter, and one-attempt execution from the Workers request-scoped compatibility port. Added focused tests that allow the reviewed Providers leaf and Workers compatibility bridge while rejecting a new provider-effect owner under Workers; the existing hosted-ownership tests reject polling/reconciliation assigned to Workers and accept Automation Hosted Sources. Burned down all eight stale misplaced-guard inventory entries, made retired entries fail validation, and expanded Providers/Workers rationale cards with present-tense ownership. No runtime behavior, public API shape, or unrelated migration changed. make ownership-inventory-check, make package-target-manifest-check, focused boundary/inventory tests, go test compilation checks, and git diff --check pass. The full internal ownership package and ownership-boundary make target retain the pre-existing Workers/Recordings root-contract and two unrelated baseline violations documented in progress.txt.

userStories.title: Reconcile canonical service-owner documentation
userStories.description: As a contributor, I want the canonical service-owner tables to agree with the reviewed inventories so that repository guidance leads changes to the correct package and contract boundary.
acceptanceCriteria: The service-owner tables in AGENTS.md, docs/architecture/architecture.md, and docs/architecture/packaged-structure.md consistently describe the implemented Worker Sessions, Events, Chat Sessions, Factory Sessions, Providers, Workers, Automations, platform, ACP transport, and mapping ownership boundaries.
The tables state that Providers owns provider inference and execution policy, Automations owns hosted polling, and Workers consumes owner contracts to perform request-scoped worker execution.

Events is described as the process-local source-native stream and Recordings as canonical Factory history; Chat Sessions and Worker Sessions are described as current implemented owners rather than future services.
Documentation uses the customer-facing Factory vocabulary defined by the data model and does not expose internal Petri terminology as a service boundary.
The package-target and ownership inventory checks still pass after the documentation reconciliation.
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
